title: X11 on Gnome issue with non-integer scaling causes main viewport render at higher resolution
body:
### Tested versions

- Godot 4.6, Linux
- Godot 4.6, Windows version running on Linux in Wine (Steam->Proton)

### System information

#### Repros:
Ubuntu+Gnome, CachyOS+Gnome

#### Does NOT Repro:
CachyOS+KDE, PopOS+Cosmic

### Issue description

#### Overview/ReproEnv

I believe there is a bug with how Godot and Gnome interact for non-integer scaling. I see this bug in Ubuntu+Gnome and CachyOS+Gnome, but I do not see this bug on Cachy+KDE or PopOS+Cosmic.
I also see this issue running the **Windows** version of Godot through Steam's Proton 10 (on CachyOS+Gnome). 

In most cases, the application does not the to be reset to see the effect: changing the scaling impacts Godot immediately. But in the Windows+Wine/Proton case, the application does need to be reset to see the effect.

The issue seems to be an Gnome+X11 issue. Forcing Wayland (with `display/display_server/driver.linuxbsd` in settings) on Gnome fixes the issue. But I still cannot repro on PopOS+Cosmic or Cachy+KDE by forcing X11. I believe Proton/Wine defaults to X11, but I did not verify that.

I expect this is reading some environment variable, which would help explain why it is reproducible with the Windows version running in Wine. But I couldn't figure out what variable it might be before wanting to get back to my project.

#### Symptoms

If scaling is 100% or 200%, scaling works fine, full screen reports exactly your current screen resolution. Fullscreen (F11) should report your screen resolution. But 125% it will report 1.6x your resolution and 166% scaling it will report 1.2x resolution.

#### Why is this important?

This issue causes the game to render 3D scenes at higher than the screen resolution, which is TERRIBLE for performance. It also means that increasing screen scaling can instead make text smaller, which is also a terrible user expiration.

### Steps to reproduce

- Run Gnome DE on Linux
- Put the below script on a label in an empty scene and run it (press F11 to toggle fullscreen).
- Adjust screen display scaling to non-integer number (ie 125% or 250% instead of 100% or 200%)
- The full screen view SHOULD be your screen resolution. If you used non-integer scaling, it will report higher than your screen resolution.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Add this script to a label on ANY project:

```gdscript
extends Label

func _ready() -> void:
    get_window().size_changed.connect(updateSize)
    updateSize()

var msg = "The window size is: %s\nPress F11 to toggle fullscreen."
func updateSize():
    var w = get_window()
    text = msg % [w.size] 

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if event is InputEventKey and event.is_pressed() and event.keycode == KEY_F11:
            var w: = get_window()
            w.mode = Window.MODE_FULLSCREEN if w.mode != Window.MODE_FULLSCREEN else Window.MODE_WINDOWED
```
